content.title: Furniture Sales Inch Up, Rooms To Go Digs Deeper Into Texas
content.subtitle: August's modest gains, Gen Z's price sensitivity and Rooms To Go's Texas build-out point to a market that is growing carefully rather than surging.
content.greeting: Good morning. Census data out this week shows furniture and home furnishings sales up just 0.9% month over month in August, the weakest showing among major retail categories even as total retail spending jumped 6% year over year. That caution shows up everywhere today: Gen Z shoppers in the new Consumer Insights Now survey say price and durability drive their decisions more than brand loyalty, Jensen Outdoor is leaning on special orders and premium accessories rather than discounting, and Rooms To Go keeps expanding in Texas anyway because growth markets still beat flat ones. Add Bread Financial's read on tightening consumer credit and Amazon's wage bump, and the thread is clear: shoppers have money but are spending it deliberately.

one_thing.headline: Stack Financing Before the Rate-Sensitive Shopper Balks
one_thing.body: With Bread Financial flagging a more cash-protective consumer and Census data showing furniture sales growth trailing the broader retail rebound, this week is the time to review the financing waterfall on the floor. Confirm that a declined first application automatically routes to a second-look or lease-to-own option rather than ending the conversation, since layered approval paths now decide whether a hesitant, value-conscious shopper walks out with or without a purchase.

content.closing: Monday's Brief will track High Point Market previews, further Consumer Insights Now data on Gen Z shopping behavior, and any fresh detail on how tariffs and supply chains are shaping fall buying decisions.
